ppbbll5 is a dependency-confusion package: its description is "Compatibility shim." and its README calls it an "authorized dependency-confusion test" by "Kero (@0xWise)". Each listed version has a postinstall script that runs `node beacon.cjs` on npm install, and index.js runs the same code when the package is imported; it POSTs the hostname, install path and current working directory to `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc` with TLS certificate checks turned off, and index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions so builds that import the real package keep running. The npm account ppblpp1 published ppbbll5 and 7 other packages with the same beacon on 2026-11-21 between 21:34 and 22:09 UTC.

## Source: amazon-inspector (08fb416c8344d431ab4fd46850476694ccf0eacac91e06cb59d2097fda6a1996)
ppbbll5 is a stub npm package whose index.js exports a Proxy returning noop functions for every property access; it ships no real functionality despite describing itself as a 'compatibility shim.' Its package.json postinstall hook executes `node beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon is invoked from index.js on require(). beacon.cjs collects the package name, os.hostname(), the install path, process.cwd(), and process.version, and POSTs them over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). The destination is a bare Contabo VPS unrelated to any legitimate publisher, and the beacon fires automatically on `npm install` and on module import, with no documented or caller-configurable purpose.
